notes.title: 5 Things To Know About Memoriapolis
notes.content:
Hello builders!

If you’re on the lookout for a game that combines city-building, history and  strategy, then Memoriapolis could be the game you’ve been waiting for. Here are five things you need to know about it!

[h3]1. A Journey Through Time : FOUR AGES, ONE CITY.[/h3]

Memoriapolis is not just a game; it's a journey through different historical eras. From the grandeur of Antiquity to the challenges of the Middle Ages, you get to build and manage a city that evolves through time. This unique feature allows you to experience the richness of various historical periods, each with its own architectural styles and cultural influences.

[b]The early access allows players to experience the first two ages: Antiquity and the Middle Ages[/b].

[h3]2. Organic growth[/h3]

Memoriapolis will not produce a regular construction grid to rely on. Thanks to our unique algorithm, overseen by an urban planner, the city develops organically to be the most realistic-looking city possible.
The residents themselves define the routes through the city as they navigate between buildings like forum, market, fortress and more.

[h3]3. Factions and Alliances[/h3]

In Memoriapolis, you have the opportunity to interact with various factions. These factions come with their own unique benefits, such as providing gold and culture points, but they also have specific needs and expectations. High trust in these factions can reduce the risk of incidents in your town, but beware, unmet expectations can lead to tensions!

[h3]4. Exclusive Early Access Content[/h3]

By joining Memoriapolis during its early access phase, you get access to exclusive content that won't be available in the final version of the game. This is the "[b]Statue of the Founders[/b]," a tribute to the pioneers of your city. This exclusive building not only enhances the aesthetics of your city but also symbolizes your early support and contribution to the game’s development.

[h3]5. More than history, it's your story![/h3]

Thanks to the 6 cultures available at the beginning of your adventure, no game will be the same. The culture you choose will impact your city and offer significant replayability. Will you choose to be a craftsman, the influence of a politician, the mind of a philosopher, or something else?
You will face historical events like the Black Death and manage internal events such as riots and strikes that could lead to losing the game!
But... as a leader, you will build a flourishing city adorned with wonders like the Great Library of Alexandria, Windsor Castle, the Leaning Tower of Pisa, the Palace of Versailles and more to showcase your wealth and power throughout the ages!

Whether you're a city-builder addict, fan of history or amateur of strategy, Memoriapolis has something to offer.

Join the Memoriapolis community and start your journey through time, builders!

notes.title: Service Buildings
notes.content:
We’ve already spoken about [b]Culture Buildings[/b] but [b]Service buildings[/b] are surely the most important buildings in your city. 

[list]
[*] They have a weak attraction but grant a lot of satisfaction!
[*] Unlike cultural buildings, they do not degrade during age changes, even if they cannot be evolved, nor unlocked and built outside their historical period.
[/list]

As soon as their construction is complete, they provide access to numerous game mechanics, depending on their culture. 

All these mechanics will evolve over the course of the city's history:
[list]
[*] The production service building is linked to the storage and management of resources.
[*] The Horreum (antiquity) provides a large storage capacity.
[*] The military service building is in charge of protecting the city, anticipating events and carrying out attacks.
[*] The Belfry (middle-ages) allows you to use army points to increase the city’s defenses.
[*] The religious service building is in charge of housing managemen.
[*] The Master builder’s office (middle-ages) allows you to modify the urban planning rules neighborgoods and integrate the wanderers.
[*] The education service building manages all the know-how learned in the ages.
[*] The Library (middle-ages) is the right place for your knowledge!
[*] The commercial service building is authorized to sell and buy various goods.
[*] Thanks to the Macellum (antiquity) you will be able to open trade routes in order to exchange resources with other cities.
[*] The politics service building allows you to pass decrees in your city.
[*] Don’t neglect the Senatus (antiquity)!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/9a8fac409807fdc7a6652b9041b71837525ad9a2.jpg[/img]The Belfry

See you soon builders!

notes.title: The bigger the better!
notes.content:
Do you know what we like about Memoriapolis? Seeing the Wonders blooming around your city! 

Wonders radiate and showcase your wealth and power throughout the ages, but their construction costs are high! So be careful with your resources because you will have to construct several Wonders throughout the ages.

Wonders have significant advantages:
[list]
[*] Lots of attraction,
[*] Cultural influence on adjacent neighborhoods,
[*] Boost of the satisfactions and more!
[/list]

But that’s not all! Wonders are prestigious buildings with their own special effects. They also function as cultural buildings and offer a security area around them. They can only be built during the corresponding age (no Circus Maximus in the Middle Ages of course ːsteamhappyː. 

Wonders are not damaged when transitioning from one age to another and their construction time does not end when an age ends.
At the end of each age, the player’s family offers to pick up the plan of a Wonder free of charge… Choose carefully the building not chosen won’t no longer be unlocked during the game!

To name just a few, you can construct: 
[list]
[*] The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus or the Circus Maximus in Antiquity, 
[*] Notre-Dame de Paris or the Charles Bridge in the Middle Ages,
[*] The Château de Chenonceau or Doge's Palace in the Renaissance,
[*] … and for the Age of Enlightenment... patience, we can't reveal everything yet!
[/list]

See you soon builders!

Hello,

The current playtest will come to an end on Sunday evening, and I thought it would be interesting to give you an update on how it's going and what players are saying.

First of all, from a quantitative point of view alone, it's much better than the first one!
Almost twice as many players tested Mémoriapolis as in the previous playtest. More players, more feedback, and a much higher average playing time.

In short, the team is very happy with this session!

Very happy, but focused on what remains to be done. 
The feedback can be divided into three main categories: crashes, zoom and new fields.

[h2]CRASHES[/h2]
There are still a lot of them. 
We are fully aware of this and the team will be concentrating on correcting them over the coming months. Some have already been corrected on our internal version, while others will be more complicated to remove. We know that this is a major challenge if we want to build a community around the game, and enable players to trust us with future developments.

[h2]THE FIELDS[/h2]
The proposal not to be able to destroy them was based on our desire to confront players with their choices. Especially as they could become neighbourhoods once the farm had been destroyed.

But it didn't work. ːsteamsadː

The team is currently testing a version with fields that can easily be destroyed according to the town's organisational needs. This has forced us to remove the possibility of fields becoming neighbourhoods initially. This option may come back later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/651788bcc34369d4da19f16ffed842c0ef29cd64.gif[/img]
[When and how much will it cost to destroy a field?

[h2]THE ZOOM[/h2]
I think this is by far the biggest demand: to be able to lower the camera.

What you have to understand is that the buildings that players put up are modelled by a talented person who has done some very fine work that could really do with being seen more closely. The houses, on the other hand, are procedurally generated and their 3D models are much more basic.

To meet this demand, we need to greatly improve these models, which is not impossible, but costly in terms of time and resources.

Once again, the person in charge of shaders is working on this, and we hope to be able to meet your expectations for the next version of the playtest, which should arrive at the end of April.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/28437dccf8dbd6454d36cad14c43c8bb7aeb407b.png[/img]
[i]Improved 3D models + objects on roofs and facades[/i].

I'd like to take this opportunity to [b]thank the players for the quality of their feedback and the kindness they've shown[/b] in their messages.

Even the most critical ones were always accompanied by a message of encouragement and that's invaluable for the whole team. So a big thank you to you all! ːsteamthumbsupː

notes.title: It's Buildredi !
notes.content:
New Friday, new version! ːsteamhappyː
As well as adding various improvements, we have integrated two main features which are: 
[list]
[*] A brand new field management system
[*] Incidents in neighbourhoods
[/list]
[h2]FIELDS[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/1496ca45ab4f3302907365eea2a535f814e28708.png[/img]

Gone are the days when houses appeared on fields!

With this new system, fields are generated in the same way as land, which means that when your town grows, they can be transformed into housing land.

Each time you set up a farm, it will generate a minimum and a maximum number of fields whose production level will depend on the level of your farm. In other words, it's up to you to decide whether to consume resources to improve the production of your fields or build another farm and lose space!

[h2]INCIDENTS[/h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/74bc49b15ad269f43fcace5e430561be9fed2f9b.jpg[/img]
Behind this generic term lies a system of faction reactions to your actions. I'll let Margaux, Game Designer, tell you more about it than I can.

[i]Incidents are the negative expressions of citizens who have been neglected for too long. 

[b]When do they appear?[/b]
The more Satisfactions are negative, the higher the probability of their appearance. Note that the more they are neglected, the higher the probability!

[b]Where do they appear?[/b]
Each neighbourhood has a risk level that is calculated using several parameters such as faction confidence, attrition zone, density, etc. The riskiest neighbourhood is therefore the first to be targeted.

[b]How do you stop them?[/b]
There's absolutely nothing you can do, apart from improve your city to prevent further incidents.

[b]How many types of incident are there?[/b]
In reality, there are two types of incident: those that can spread and become a real ordeal for your citizens, and others that only last for a cycle.
Fires and epidemics fall into the first category. While the former will destroy your citizens' homes, the latter will drastically reduce your population.
Assaults and robberies fall into the second category. The former will reduce the confidence/satisfaction of your citizens/factions, and the latter will have a direct impact on your resource reserves. [/i]

Thanks Margaux. ːsteamthumbsupː

See you next week.

notes.title: Town planning rules
notes.content:
Today we're going to take a little time to explain in detail what we've called the "town planning rules" in Memoriapolis and how you'll be able to interact with them.

A planning rule defines how land and houses are created in the game.
They concern 

[list]
[*] The size and shape of the plot
[*] How the land is divided into blocks and the size of the paths that divide it up
[*] The size and length of properties
[*] The type of house (facade, roof, colour)
[*] Treatment of open spaces (garden, green space, trees)
[*] The percentage of built and open space
[/list]
These town planning rules are obviously modified when moving from one age to another, but also within the same age, [b]when the player develops his town centre.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/bcc964b014ab064d22cd82497dbaa40627b6e058.jpg[/img][i]Evolution of the town centre in ancient times[/i]

[b]The town centre is the first building of an age.[/b]

This is the building that will define the area in which you will be allowed to build in Antiquity, or the safety area in the Middle Ages. This building can evolve over 5 levels, which give access to specific bonuses and, at levels 1 and 3, change the town planning rules for the current age.

There are therefore 4 town planning rules in the Early Access version of the game (Antiquity and the Middle Ages) and 8 in the final version of the game, which adds the Renaissance and the Age of Enlightenment.

First of all, let's explain how to define the place where a plot of land is created.

Every time the player places a building on the map, it affects the city's drawing power. This force of attraction, which affects the whole city, defines where the next plots of land will be created. All the buildings you place on the map have their own attraction force. It will add to, or sometimes subtract from, the force of attraction already present.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/df7f91fa39d280298f8b6f5fd42cff4a57f25378.gif[/img]

We'll be coming back to the details of how the attraction works in another Dev Diary. 

Now that a new building has been constructed, it will allow the arrival of new building plots in the city.

A plot of land is an area of variable shape and size that is positioned to be as close as possible to the nearest source of attraction. The land is divided into blocks, which are in turn divided into properties. The houses will be built on these properties.

The size of the plots and the size of the properties are values defined by the town planning rules of the current age. This division is specific to the current age and will be different for each age of the game. 

[b]The way a plot of land is divided into parcels is a fixed feature, regardless of the current age.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/ee09658499c45a4c468ae204e87495c17ebafcb6.jpg[/img][i]Parceling in Antiquity[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/532c971fce07d1804055cdb05798b4b187f32ed7.jpg[/img][i]Parceling in Middle Ages[/i]

A plot of land created in early antiquity can have its dwellings transformed as the town evolves towards other town planning rules, but this will not change the organisation of its properties. This is not possible during Antiquity, but players will have a way of remedying this from the Middle Ages onwards.

With the "Master Builder's Office" building, players can influence the town planning rules and modify certain aspects, in particular the density of buildings, the maximum height of dwellings or the division of properties. These changes will obviously have a cost.

[b]To conclude on the subject of town planning rules, I think it's important to say that ideally you shouldn't see them![/b]

In fact, our aim was to make the development of the town seem as realistic as possible, as organic as possible, and as logical as possible, and to make the transformations of your town at each age seem normal.

Time will tell whether we've succeeded.

In the next Dev Diary we'll explain how to win or lose.

notes.title: Resources
notes.content:
There are six basic resources: 
[list]
[*] wood, 
[*] stone, 
[*] sand,
[*] clay 
[*] iron 
[*] gold.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/27b02483cf4e386a2ce19cc90fc73730d45d0f06.jpg[/img]
They can be transformed into : 
[list]
[*] beams, 
[*] rubble,  
[*] tiles, 
[*] bricks, 
[*] steel,
[*] jewellery.
[/list]
There are special resources such as gold coins, gems, blueprints, food and culture points, which are not used to construct buildings but for many other tasks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44588238/7d6d0aa9fbd30ec2da21a5ee8300ec90dc515209.jpg[/img][i]A farm and its fields on the edge of town[/i]

We wanted to use a fairly varied number of resources to create different ways of occupying natural space with harvesting buildings, but not overdo it to keep the game accessible. Production is an important part of developing a town, but we didn't want it to be the focus of the game.

[b]Tip[/b]: Make sure you always produce more food than you consume. As citizens continue to flock to your city, this is bound to happen eventually, and you don't want a famine to break out! ːsteamfacepalmː
